models_evaluated: 3 previously described fall prediction models based on questionnaires and trunk accelerometry

links.outcome: Fall prediction model performance in external cohort versus original cohort
links.effect: All models showed poor precision (0.20-0.49), poor sensitivity (0.32-0.58), and specificity 0.45-0.89 in the external cohort; odds ratios differed from the original cohort.
links.quote: Fall risk prediction in our cohort was not as effective as in the original cohort.

links.outcome: Model accuracy after recalibration or re-optimizing parameters on the external cohort
links.effect: Recalibration of the original models had limited effect on performance; optimized coefficients and cutoffs also gave limited benefit.
links.quote: Recalibration as well as optimized model parameters resulted in a limited increase in accuracy.

links.effect: External precision 0.20-0.49, sensitivity 0.32-0.58, specificity 0.45-0.89; prediction was not as effective as original cohort.
links.quote: All models showed poor precision (0.20-0.49), poor sensitivity (0.32-0.58), and good specificity (0.45-0.89).

links.effect: Odds ratios differed; gait characteristics except harmonicity ML were not statistically associated with falls.
links.quote: Lastly, the odds ratios in our cohort were different from those in the original cohort, which indicated that gait characteristics, except for the index of harmonicity ML (medial-lateral direction), were not statistically associated with falls.
